ida (oncall): prod SSO unexplained 401s since 02:14 UTC. Affected ~5% of logins, all OIDC flows (code->token). sample error: invalid_grant on /oauth/token. Anyone else seeing this? :eyes:

alex (eng-sec): looking now. any commonality in users? org or role?

ida (oncall): seemed to start right after the RBAC role rename rollout (roles/frontend -> roles/web). Not all users in that org, roughly those who recently got the new role mapped via SCIM.

sam (platform): can you paste the token-exchange response body we got from the idp?

ida (oncall): sure, from one failing exchange:

HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
content-type: application/json
{
  "error": "invalid_grant",
  "error_description": "token exchange failed: aud mismatch (expected 'redwood-api' got 'redwood-inference')"
}

maria (sre): aud mismatch is interesting. We didn't change the client_id for the backend. Did the IDP rotate the JWKs or the trust anchor earlier? KMS rewrap job ran ~02:10 UTC (logs show alias swap).

alex (eng-sec): KMS rewrap could change envelope metadata. If the IDP signs assertions using a key that the token-exchange service verifies via JWK set cached locally, and we rewrapped the signing key in KMS, the kid might have changed. But the error says aud mismatch, not sig. Could be a claim-mapping config in the SSO connector that was updated during the RBAC rename.

ida (oncall): we ran a canary mapping job that updated SCIM role->claim mapping to emit 'roles.web' as claim 'roles' instead of 'app_roles'. Maybe the token-exchange service expects claims in 'app_roles' and falls back to audience selection logic that picks a different audience when mapping absent. That would be a brittle heuristic.

sam (platform): reproducing locally: exchange with id_token payload where claim 'aud' = ["redwood-inference"], our backend expects single-string aud 'redwood-api'. The token-exchange route checks aud equality strictly. Why would aud change? upstream IDP client config might have multiple audience targets configured.

alex (eng-sec): check IDP client settings for the OAuth client used by the web app. Also look at the SAML->OIDC bridge mapping if this org uses SAML IdPs. If SCIM changed role names, a provisioning webhook might have triggered an automated client update (we have that automation in onboarding).

maria (sre): KMS-bot shows rewrap job at 02:09:58 UTC for alias alias/idp-signing-key -> alias/idp-signing-key-v2 with in-flight requests. Recent audit log snippet:

kms-bot: rewrap alias/idp-signing-key -> alias/idp-signing-key-v2 by infra-deploy (ci-run-421)
context: propagation=false, rotate_jwk=true

ida (oncall): propagation=false looks suspicious 1 means the deployment didn't wait for global propagation. That could leave some validators checking the old kid and some the new one. But again: logs show aud mismatch rather than sig failure. Maybe the token exchange falls back to a different downstream client when signature verification fails, and that other client has aud 'redwood-inference'.

sam (platform): ok next steps: 1) pin IDP JWKs from cache to live fetch (bypass cache) for a minute and run synthetic exchange, 2) roll back the SCIM claim mapping change for the affected orgs, 3) check oauth client config for audience aliases. I'll open a quick runbook.

alex (eng-sec): also add an audit trail query: search auth.audit for token-exchange errors and include idp.kid, oauth.client_id, and scim.role_version. If we see mismatched kid combined with aud mismatch, that confirms cascade.

ida (oncall): I ran the audit query and found 12 entries between 02:14-02:22 with pattern: error=invalid_grant aud=["redwood-inference"] client_id=svc-web-app scim_role_version=2026-03-23T02:09:00Z idp_kid=abcd1234

maria (sre): another set shows idp_kid=efgh5678 for successful exchanges at same time window. Two kids in rotation overlap 1 matches propagation=false.

sam (platform): mitigation: 1) pause the rewrap propagation (abort), 2) revert SCIM mapping change for the subset, 3) roll out a strict aud check tolerant-mode that accepts arrays and either audience if context matches (short lived).

alex (eng-sec): we should avoid changing aud semantics 1 instead fix upstream: ensure IDP clients and our token-exchange agree on aud format. As a hotfix accept array aud if one of them matches 'redwood-api' and log a high-severity audit event.

ida (oncall): applying hotfix to canary now (will accept array aud). Also paused KMS rewrap propagation via infra toggle. patch in canary in ~5m.

kms-bot: action=abort_rewrap alias=alias/idp-signing-key-v2 requested_by=sam result=queued

maria (sre): canary hotfix looks good, synthetic tests passing for exchanges. rolling to prod in 10m. We should schedule a postmortem once stabilized to discuss: - KMS rewrap propagation=false risk - SCIM->claim mapping orchestration and feature flags - stronger audit signals when aud/signature mismatch cascade

alex (eng-sec): agreed. I'll open an incident with Sev3->investigation and link this thread. Please add any relevant logs to the incident doc.

ida (oncall): thanks team. Will keep monitoring. :thumbsup:
